feature: An edited recording comes out as a video file
summary: Export on a document that has time now writes a video of what plays in the window: the pieces in the order they are in, the ones you threw away absent, everything drawn over the picture, and the mix you hear on space. A recording nobody has touched still goes out as a straight copy of its own file, so what was instant stays instant.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Turn on "A recording opens in the editor you already know", "Cut a recording", "Sound on the timeline" and "An edited recording comes out as a video file" (all on by default in Next except the first). Open any screen recording.

try.do: Press ⇧⌘E on the recording as it opened. The sheet says MP4 · the file's exact size, because nothing has been edited yet.
Press Export…, save it, then play the file that landed. It is the recording, byte for byte: nothing was re-encoded.
Put the playhead in the middle, press B to cut the clip, then press ⌫ to throw the piece under the playhead away.
Draw a rectangle over the video with the Rectangle tool.
Press ⇧⌘E again and export. The file runs half as long, starts where the kept piece starts, and the box is over every frame of it.
Add a sound with Audio ▸ Add Sound, pull its level down, then export again and listen: the music is in the file at the level you set, under the recording's own sound.
Pick GIF on the sheet. The size presets appear, the same ones a recording already offers, and the line underneath says the size comes with the file.

evaluate: When you press Export on a recording, is a video obviously what you expected to get?
The card that counts up while it writes: does it tell you enough, and is Stop where you would look for it?
Is it fast enough to not think about? Four seconds of 1280 x 800 took about 1.3 seconds on this machine.
The sheet says "size not known until it is written" for anything edited. Is that honesty useful, or would a rough number be better than none?
A document whose music runs past its last clip ends in black. Is that what you would expect, or should the picture hold on its last frame?
rough: Export on a document with time is the video sheet only, so the still PNG of one frame that Export used to write is not reachable from there. Nobody has asked for it; when somebody does it is a fourth row on the same sheet, not a second sheet.

MP4 has no quality choice, on purpose: that is the separate task a-recording-can-be-made-small-enough-to-send, and a second set of answers to the same question is exactly what this task was told not to invent.

The Stop button on the progress card is not driven by a scripted walk: exports of the sample finish in about a second, so there is nothing for a walk to catch mid-flight. The half that matters is tested — cancelling the writer throws and leaves no file behind — but the button itself was checked by reading it, not by pressing it.
The export borrows the window's picture store for the frames it decodes and gives every one back as it goes. While it runs, the canvas can lose a frame it was holding and has to fetch it again.
A long recording is a long export: every frame is a decode plus a composite. Nothing is parallel yet, and nothing has been measured past fourteen seconds of document.
